📝A Hasid in the Trenches?📝
Upon seeing [mountains of garbage](https://t.me/rybar/83041) left by Middle Eastern pilgrims in Uman during the celebration of the Jewish New Year, many Ukrainians probably wished they could take it out on the tourists. And their dream, it seems, has partly come true.
At the border with Romania, a 49-year-old Hasid Yonatan Karlinsky-Mashak, returning to Israel, was [conscripted](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-909158). Although he left so-called Ukraine 14 years ago, and his passport lists the USSR as his birthplace, border guards "identified" him by his knowledge of the language and removed him from the flight.
The Israeli Foreign Ministry, usually quick to respond to far less serious incidents involving its citizens abroad, remains silent. And the wife of the abducted man is oddly more concerned that in the hands of the TCC he cannot eat kosher food.
📌 But the most amusing thing is that absolutely any outcome of this episode will, albeit slightly, hurt precisely so-called Ukraine. If the detained Hasid is sent to the AFU, it will further change the attitude of part of the Jewish community toward the Kyiv regime.
And if this Israeli is simply released, Ukrainians will once again be made to understand that they are fundamentally second-class people. They will increasingly be haunted by thoughts like "we are sent to the front so that they can not fear the TCC and lord it over our lands."
So we await the resolution of this story — it will clearly provide a couple of very vivid news hooks.

events.text:
🪖 Ethiopian rebels advance, threatening to destabilize East Africa amid Gulf crisis
Tigrayan rebels in northern Ethiopia are clashing with federal forces after launching a major offensive on September 23.
The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and aligned forces reportedly seized control of Alula Aba Nega Airport in Mekelle, as well as airports in Axum and Shire.
🔴 In neighboring Afar, clashes with federal forces were reported in Abala and Erebti. The TPLF also reportedly took control of Berhale, Megale, Dalul and Konoba
🔴 The Amhara region has also been targeted by the TPLF
🔴 Fighting was reported around the Amhara town of Weldiya, one of the few routes to the capital, Addis Ababa
The rebels aim to take Addis Ababa, while the offensive in Afar could seek to cut off supplies from Djibouti, which handles most of Ethiopia’s international trade cargo, experts say.
Videos appearing to show captured federal troops and military equipment are circulating on social media.
The unfolding conflict could affect Sudan, Eritrea, Somalia and the wider Red Sea region, Reuters reports.
The US Embassy in Addis Ababa has barred US government personnel from traveling to Tigray and Afar and advised American citizens in the conflict zone to shelter in place until it is safe to leave.
Ethiopia’s federal government and the TPLF fought a 2020-2022 civil war that claimed more than 600,000 lives. The TPLF dominated Ethiopia’s government from 1991 to 2018, before Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed came to power.
